devdoc.details: How one month runs for one pair:      1. Lock. On the 15th at 00:00 UTC+8 the pair's round locks. Plans in it cannot top up or cancel until it         settles, and new plans join next month's round instead.      2. `startRound`. A keeper redeems the round's stable from the yield source and sends the fee to the Reserve.         The fee is a share of the interest only, never of principal.      3. `swapRoundPart`. The keeper swaps that stable for the asset in 1 to `maxParts` parts through SwapHelper,         on routes built and signed off chain. Each part must return at least the keeper's fresh quote less         `maxSlippageBps`, and that minimum can be at most `maxOracleDeviationBps` below the oracle value.      4. `settleRound`. The asset bought is supplied to its yield source and the round closes.      No round or plan call loops over the plans of a pair. Every plan sells the same number of stable units in each of its buys, so a pair      only stores the totals of its next round (`roundStableUnits`, `roundPrincipal`). Settling a round adds the      asset bought per stable unit sold to a running index, and a plan's asset is its units per buy times how much      the index grew over its rounds. A plan that starts or ends in a later round is added to or removed from the      totals when the round before it settles, through that round's `stableUnitsJoining` and `stableUnitsEnding`.      So their gas does not grow with the number of plans a pair has. `transferPlan` is the one call that walks      a list: the owner's plan ids.      SmartDCA never borrows and never enables a market as collateral, so nothing it holds can be liquidated.      {SmartDCAAdminLib} is linked for EIP-170 headroom; a library declares no state, so it cannot shift this layout.

cancelPlan(uint256,bool,address).details: The fee is `feeRateBps` of what the waiting stable redeems above its principal, so a cancel never takes a      fee from principal. Reverts if the plan is in a round past its lock time that has not settled, or if      every buy has settled (claim it instead).      With `toCore`, the bought asset is paid as the asset's Core vTokens; reverts with `NotCoreSource` if the      asset side is not in Core and the plan has bought asset. Use it when Core cannot redeem the asset, for      example with too little cash or redeem paused: without `toCore` the whole cancel reverts, the stable too.

params.toCore: True to pay the bought asset as vTokens, false to pay it as the asset

claimPlan(uint256,bool,address).details: With `toCore`, `receiver` gets the asset's Core vTokens and keeps earning; collateral is not enabled for      them. Up to `scheduleBuys - 1` stable units are left by rounding the per-buy amount down and are dropped      here; each is worth about one share of the first source the stable side used (under 1 wei for a Hub,      about 2e8 wei for a Core vToken).      With `toCore`, reverts with `NotCoreSource` if the asset side is not in Core.

params.toCore: True to pay as vTokens, false to pay as the asset

params.swapHelper: SwapHelper that runs the signed swap multicall

createPlan(uint32,uint256,uint8,address).details: The caller pays and must first `approve` SmartDCA for `amount` of the stable; `owner` can be another      address, so a contract can open a plan for a user. The deposit goes into the pair's stable      source and the plan holds units of it. Each buy sells the same number of units, so a buy's stable amount      grows with the interest earned while waiting.      The plan's first round is the pair's next round when called before that round's lock time, and the round      after it from the lock time on. During an overrun (a round still running past the next 15th) that is the      round right after the running one, not the calendar month.      Reverts if `owner` is the zero address, if the pair is unknown or disabled, if `buys` is outside `minBuys`      to `maxBuys`, or if the stable received is under `minAmountPerBuy` of the stable times `buys`. The stable      received is counted as a balance change, so for a token that charges a transfer fee it is below `amount`.

params.amount: Stable amount to deposit, in the stable's decimals

forceBuy(uint32,uint8).details: Callable from `FALLBACK_DELAY` (24 h) after the round's start until it settles; before that it reverts with      `RoundNotStarted`, carrying the time it opens. For a crisis such as the keeper or the backend being down. The swap needs no signed route:      it approves only the part's stable, calls the router's `exactInput`, and reverts if the router took less      than the part or if the asset that arrived is below the oracle value of the part less      `fallbackSlippageBps`. `parts = 1` runs the whole round in one call; a large round can take more parts, sent      apart, so each one moves the pool less. The keeper can keep running the same round, since both share its      part count, and a round whose parts are all swapped only settles. The router is the PancakeSwap V3      SwapRouter, and `fallbackSlippageBps` starts at 0.5%.      On a round that has started, `parts` below the parts left cuts the parts left to `parts`; a higher value      or 0 keeps them. A round the keeper started in 50 parts finishes in one call with `parts = 1`, and calling      again with the same `parts` swaps the next part.

params.parts: Parts to split the round into, 1 to `maxParts`; on a started round, the most parts to leave

returns._0: Plan ids, including cancelled and claimed plans; a transfer changes their order

initialize(address,address).details: Fee rate 0 with a cap of 20%, slippage bound 0.1%, up to 10 parts per round, 2 to 60 buys per plan, a      0.5% slippage bound for `forceBuy`, and a keeper swap's `minOut` at most 1% below the oracle value

nextLockTime(uint32).details: Read from stored state, so on a pair with empty rounds not settled yet it can be in the past, and a plan      created now joins a later round. An unknown `pairId` returns the lock time of round 1.

returns._0: Unix timestamp of the 15th at 00:00 UTC+8 of that round's month

params.router: PancakeSwap V3 SwapRouter, zero to remove the route

params.newMaxSlippageBps: New bound in basis points, up to `MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS`

setMinAmountPerBuy(address,uint256).details: Must be set before the stable's first pair is added.

params.newAmount: New minimum in the stable's decimals, above 0

params.enabled: True to allow new plans and top ups

setYieldSource(uint32,uint8,uint8,addres.details: Plans hold units, and the move keeps the number of units, so no plan changes. A stable side that holds      shares cannot move from its next round's lock time until that round settles (`PairLocked`); an asset      move can, as a running round holds its bought asset as tokens. Empty rounds whose lock time has passed      are settled first, so they do not block the move. Works while paused.

params.source: A Hub registered in the Hub registry for the side's token, or a Core vToken listed in the        Comptroller whose underlying is that token

settleRound(uint32).details: Reverts while the asset's source refuses the deposit (a Core supply cap or a mint pause); the keeper      retries until it goes through. Rounds with nothing to buy that are already past their lock time are      settled right after.

startRound(uint32,uint8).details: Keepers can call from the round's lock time.      Rounds with nothing to buy are settled first. If the round after them is not locked yet, the call returns      with nothing done.      The fee is `feeRateBps` of what the round redeems above its principal, and the rate is fixed for the      round here. Reverts if the round already started, or if the redeem returns nothing.

params.parts: Parts to split the swap into, 1 to `maxParts`

swapRoundPart(uint32,uint256,bytes).details: Each part sells an even share of what is left, `stableToSwap / parts left`, so the last part sells the      rest. `quotedOut` less `maxSlippageBps` is the swap's `minOut`, and it may be at most      `maxOracleDeviationBps` below the oracle value of the part (`QuoteBelowOracle`). The swap must return at      least `minOut`, and the whole part must be sold:      no stable may come back to SmartDCA or stay in SwapHelper. Every `genericCall` target and `approveMax`      spender in the multicall must be on `allowedRouters`, and every `sweep` must send the pair's stable or      asset to SmartDCA.

params.quotedOut: Fresh quote for this part's stable, in the asset's decimals, with pool fees already taken;        must not be 0
params.swapData: `SwapHelper.multicall` calldata built off chain for this part and signed for SmartDCA as the        caller. It must sell the part's stable and send the asset to SmartDCA.

sweepToken(address,address).details: Owed is the source shares held for plans, and the stable or asset a running round holds between      `startRound` and `settleRound`.

topUpPlan(uint256,uint256).details: Caller must own the plan and first `approve` SmartDCA for `amount`. The schedule restarts: what was bought      so far is kept aside, and the stable still waiting plus the new deposit is split evenly over the buys left.      Reverts if the plan is in a round past its lock time that has not settled, if every buy has settled, if      the pair is disabled, or if the stable received, counted as a balance change, is under `minAmountPerBuy`      times the buys left.

params.amount: Stable amount to add, in the stable's decimals

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner.

transferPlan(uint256,address).details: Only the owner changes; no funds or round totals move, so it works during a lock too.

withdrawBought(uint256,uint256,bool,addr.details: Allowed while the plan's round is running: a running round's buy only counts once it settles. A partial      amount is converted to units rounded up, so `receiver` gets at least `amount`, unless Core takes a      redeem fee (`treasuryPercent`). Only the owner can call.      With `toCore`, the asset is paid as the asset's Core vTokens worth at least `amount`, and no redeem fee      applies; reverts with `NotCoreSource` if the asset side is not in Core. Use it when Core cannot redeem the      asset, for example with too little cash or redeem paused.

params.amount: Asset amount to withdraw, in the asset's decimals, also with `toCore`
params.toCore: True to pay as vTokens, false to pay as the asset

__gap.details: Storage gap for future upgrades; with the 13 slots above, SmartDCA's own state takes 50 slots

userdoc.notice: Dollar cost averaging from a stable (USDT, USDC or U) into an asset (BTCB, ETH or WBNB). A user deposits         once and picks how many monthly buys to make. Until each buy, the deposit earns interest in the pair's         stable source (a Liquidity Hub at launch). Once a month a keeper buys for every plan of a pair at once, and         the asset bought is supplied to the pair's asset source (Core at launch), where it keeps earning until         the user takes it out. Each pair has its own two sources, set by governance.
